patterns.title: Lighter than Air Shawl - 4 Shafts
patterns.description: Full 472-end striped-linen warp and both published shaft-count options. Warp stripes follow Figure 1; weft color stripes follow Figure 4, with each color stripe repeated three times and alternated with half-bleached linen. Use the source beat adjustments to square the differing linen yarns.

patterns.title: Cherry Blossom Scarf
patterns.description: Published 180-heddle mohair threading with plain-weave side panels and a doubleweave center. The doubled selvedge ends and denting groups are source loom instructions; this chart retains one assignment per heddle. The nine displayed picks repeat for 66 inches.

patterns.title: Create Sashiko Weaving Drafts with Ease - Worked Example
patterns.kind: Plain weave with supplemental warp and weft
patterns.description: The article’s complete 35-end threading and 25-pick treadling example, transcribed from its spelled-out numeric sequences. It uses the Sashiko Trails tie-up as directed, reduced to the six shafts this example needs. Monochrome ground and outline colors are illustrative; the article does not specify yarn colors for this example.

patterns.title: Sashiko Trails Table Linens - Placemat 1
patterns.kind: Plain weave with supplemental warp and weft
patterns.description: Full 236-end placemat threading with the separately printed sashiko treadling. All numbered brackets are expanded. Hem and border shed pairs marked only in inches are shown once; repeat them to the source length. Four Alabaster ground picks alternate with one Peach Harvest supplementary pattern pick.

patterns.kind: Plain weave with supplemental warp and weft
patterns.description: Complete 166-end runner threading and all five sashiko panels in their printed order. Numeric repeat brackets are expanded. Hem and border pairs specified only in inches are represented once; repeat those pairs to the source length. The source runner is about 58 inches long.

patterns.title: Sugar Plum Lace Scarf
patterns.designer: Susan Du Bois; woven by Robin Wilton
patterns.description: Complete 413-heddle threading (the two unthreaded floating selvedges are not included), with the 82-pick Swedish-lace repeat and the displayed starting and ending plain-weave picks. As printed, this rising-shed version shows warp floats on the upper face; the source derives it from Johann D’s Lace #32 in Davison.

patterns.title: Shades of Flax Towels - Towel 1
patterns.kind: Canvas weave and plain weave with color-and-weave
patterns.description: Full 268-heddle colored canvas-weave threading and Towel 1 treadling, with the six printed 12x sections expanded. The floating selvedges remain loom instructions. Hem pairs marked only in inches are shown once; extend them to the printed length.

patterns.title: Shades of Flax Towels - Towel 2
patterns.kind: Canvas weave and plain weave with color-and-weave
patterns.description: Full 268-heddle colored threading and Towel 2, including its continued outer 3x treadling bracket. Numeric repeats are expanded across both printed columns. The inch-marked hems are represented by their shown shed pairs.

patterns.title: Shades of Flax Towels - Towel 3
patterns.kind: Canvas weave and plain weave with color-and-weave
patterns.description: Full 268-heddle colored threading and Towel 3, including the continued outer 2x bracket and the second-repeat jump to the final hem. Numeric repeats are expanded. Length-only hem and stripe pairs are represented once; use the printed inch lengths at the loom.

patterns.title: Mosaic Tiles Scarf
patterns.description: Full 277-heddle threading and the complete colored-weft order from Figures 1–3. The threading bracket continues through the second row; the source adds separate floating selvedges. Eight cycles of the six 45-pick colors are followed by Blue Purple and Lemon Drop, with single Navy dividing picks and four-pick plain-weave ends.

patterns.title: City Circuits Scarf
patterns.description: Full 504-end threading and complete initial, center, balance, and ending sections. Nested numeric brackets are expanded. The center motif is woven six times; the last repeat skips its final treadling block as printed. English Rose and Teal have independent layer selvedges; correct shuttle routing and a soft beat are essential. The flat draft cannot show the relaxation of the finished deflected doubleweave.
